title: refactor(ci): unify build, lint and test workflows; optimize cache & parallelism
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: CI pipelines have drifted over time: duplicated workflow logic across repo, inefficient cache keys causing misses, and over-parallelized matrix jobs increasing queue time. This PR consolidates the canonical build/test/lint workflows into a smaller set of reusable workflows, reduces redundant matrix axes, improves cache key hygiene, and adds a small suite of annotations/telemetry for flaky-job detection. Scope: primarily the redwood monorepo workflows, with smaller hygiene updates to redwood-helm-charts and redwood-sdk-python to adopt the new workflow templates. Checklist:
- [x] Consolidate build+test into .github/workflows/ci.yml (reusable jobs used by other repos)
- [x] Consolidate lint jobs into .github/workflows/lint.yml with faster incremental linting
- [x] Reduce matrix cartesian product where not needed (node versions vs target OS)
- [x] Standardize actions/cache keys and add cache restore fallbacks
- [x] Add concurrency groups to prevent duplicate runs for the same PR branch
- [x] Add lightweight telemetry (annotations) for identifying flaky tests
- [x] Update release automation to use the unified pipeline and a smaller release matrix
- [x] Run full CI and verify all jobs pass
Related: Linear ENG-2345, ENG-2988. Also addresses hygiene flagged in ENG-3120. This is a repo-hygiene change with no behavior impact to production code. Detailed changes and rationale are in the commits summary below.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) refactor(ci): introduce reusable workflow templates and unify job names; 2) ci: optimize cache keys and add concurrency; 3) docs: update CONTRIBUTING.md and workflow references. Each commit keeps changes scoped and reversible.
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows and improved caching/parallelism. No runtime changes. Expect reduced CI latency and fewer cache misses.
conversation: Review summary: Marcus requested splitting one long 'build' job into two smaller steps to make cache boundaries explicit; addressed in commit 2. Riley requested metrics for flaky tests (annotations); I added lightweight annotations and a short telemetry script. Priya flagged a flaky integration test; we added a conditional that runs the flaky test only on the release matrix and created a follow-up ticket (ENG-3301). CI: initial run showed a failing lint job due to an older node 14 action; updated action versions and reran. Final CI passed. Approvals: Marcus approved, Riley approved, Priya approved. Notes: we intentionally kept the reusable templates minimal to avoid creating tight coupling between repos; other repos can opt into the templates via the README.
notes: Observed CI run-time improvement ~18% on average across PRs in the canary branch after reducing matrix sizes and improving cache keys. Cache hit rate increased on first restore for deterministic installs. Follow-ups: ENG-3301 (flaky-integration-test triage), ENG-3310 (expand telemetry on flaky tests), and a later PR to migrate remaining repos to the templates.
testing_plan: Validated by running the full workflow on main against the feature branch, and manual run for redwood-sdk-python. Also ran a smoke test of release automation by creating a dry-run release in a staging tag. Observed no regressions.
impact_scope: Primarily CI infra and developer velocity. No production code changes. Some downstream repos will need small updates to opt into reusable templates.
extra_context: This PR is part of the broader CI modernization initiative (ENG-2345). We are aiming to reduce CI costs and lead time while keeping workflows auditable and easy to opt into from other repos. The templates are intentionally documented with migration steps in the updated CONTRIBUTING.md.
